And when Mu'tasim heard, he sent Afshin, the general, with gifts to Stephanos,
and he took Babak and killed him.
For this man had destroyed more than one hundred thousand of the army of the Arabs.
And in the year 1149 [838 AD],
Mu'tasim entered the territory of the Romans from the Cilician Gates {OCR?} of Tarsus with twenty thousand [men],
and he sent Afshin the general with thirty thousand from the other side.
And when Mu'tasim reached the city of Nicaea,
he found it empty,
and he tore down its walls.
And from there he came to Ancyra,
and likewise he found no one in it,
because they had fled to Amorium, the great city;
and he tore down the wall of Ancyra.
Now Theophilus the emperor came against Afshin,
and he destroyed about three thousand of the Arabs.
And immediately God—glory be to His grace!—sent a violent rain.
And when Theophilus withdrew to one side with two thousand men,
the rest of the Romans supposed that the emperor had been killed,
and they fled to Constantinople.
And when the rain ceased and the air cleared {OCR?},
the numerous forces of Afshin surrounded the two thousand [men] of Theophilus;
and they were not able to overcome them until they brought mangonels to stone them.
And then the Romans rushed out, killing and being killed;
they broke through the ranks of the Arabs and escaped.
And because evening had overtaken him,
the Romans lit fires {OCR?} at night around their camp,
and set out hastily for Amorium.
And immediately a messenger arrived from the mother of Theophilus, saying:
"The Romans who have arrived have spread the report that you have been killed,
and they are seeking to appoint an emperor;
hasten and come!"
Then Theophilus encouraged the garrison of Amorium,
and gave orders, and its gates were blocked up;
and he left it as if on the edge of a razor {OCR?},
and went to Constantinople,
and killed the leaders who had desired to appoint an emperor.
Mu'tasim, however, when he had not derived any benefit from his expedition, was remorseful and said:
"We have not done well to enter here;"
and he set his face to depart.
Then a certain Ahmad, his confidant, said:
"It is not fitting for a king like you to depart empty-handed;
behold, the city of Amorium is not far from us,
let us go and capture it."
